chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Five people are not given anything from the Zakat: the father, and the mother, and the child, and the slave, and the wife; and that is because they are his dependents who are obligatory upon him.
ai.seo_question: Who are the five people who cannot receive Zakat from their own provider according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'double benefit' exclusion, where dependents whose maintenance (nafaqah) is already obligatory upon the payer cannot receive Zakat from him, preventing the substitution of obligatory charity with voluntary charity. The five excluded categories—parents, children, slaves, and wives—are considered '‘iyāl' (dependents) whose upkeep is a fixed duty, distinguishing this ruling from the general distribution to the eight categories in Surah At-Tawbah. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence in determining the eligibility of close relatives for Zakat funds.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Five should not be given anything from the Zakāt – The father, and the mother, and the children, and the owned slavers, and the wife – and that is because they are his dependants, hanging on to him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd al- Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Zakat cannot be given to five kinds of people: father, mother, children, slaves, and one’s wife, because they are one’s dependents for whom one must provide sustenance.’”
